summary: A dynastic caliphate centered on Damascus that expanded from the Atlantic region to the Indus Valley.
currency: Gold dinar and silver dirham, including the epigraphic coinage developed under Abd al-Malik.
rulers: Selected rulers: Muawiya I, 661–680; Abd al-Malik, 685–705; al-Walid I, 705–715.
economy: Unified coinage and administrative institutions strengthened central rule across diverse provincial economies.
military: Successive conquests expanded caliphal territory across North Africa and into Iberia and South Asia.
contributions: Arabic administration, reformed coinage and monuments including the Dome of the Rock helped shape early Islamic institutional and artistic traditions.
origin: Muawiya established dynastic authority after the first civil war and Ali’s assassination.
decline: The Abbasids replaced Umayyad rule in 750; a separate Umayyad dynasty later ruled in Iberia.
periodNote: 661–750 describes the Damascus-based caliphate, not the later emirate and caliphate of Córdoba.
